e1-1: This is schoolhub.adalintech.com, where every school starts. Along the top, How it works walks you through a full term with SchoolHub, from resumption to vacation. Pricing shows what it costs, per student, per term. Log in is for schools already using SchoolHub, and Start free creates a brand-new school. Further down, the page explains each part one by one: attendance, results, fees, parents and setup. Everyone at the school sees only their own part. The pricing section shows four plans, all charged per student, per term. The Free plan covers up to fifty students, and Standard and Premium both come with a free thirty-day trial. At the bottom, the footer has sign-in links for parents and students, along with our privacy notice and terms.
e1-2: To create your school, click Start free. You only need five details about yourself and your school. Before you continue, read the terms of use, the privacy notice and the data processing agreement, then tick to accept them. If your school is already on SchoolHub, use the Log in link instead. The Free plan covers up to fifty students, and you don't need a card to start. Click create, and your school is ready straight away. A welcome email is also on its way to your inbox.
e1-3: A new school opens on a short setup checklist, in the order that works best. First, your school's details and logo. Second, classes, subjects and terms. Third, invite your staff. Fourth, add your students. Each step ticks itself off as you finish it.
e1-4: Every page lives in the menu on the left, grouped by what it's for. Open a group, like Academics, Teaching, Student life, Communication, Finance or Administration, to see the pages inside it. To jump straight to a page, press Control K and type part of its name. If a page has a lock, your plan doesn't include it yet, and you'll see what it would unlock. And if you're ever stuck, ask Kola, at the bottom right. Kola explains how to do anything, for your role.
e1-5: Staff log in with their work email and password. If you're new, there's a link to create a free school account. Parents have their own sign-in, with no password at all. Schools that use Google or Microsoft accounts can sign in with those instead. Forgot your password? Request a reset link, and it arrives by email. It works for one hour.
e1-6: Click your name at the bottom left to open your account. Here you can change your name, change your password, and sign out of every device at once if you lose a phone. You can also disconnect Google or Microsoft sign-in here.
e1-7: If you run more than one school, pick one here. You can add up to five schools to the same login, and each keeps its own records and plan. Name the new school and create it, then switch between schools from the top of the menu.
e2-1: The overview is the first page you see each day. The Today tab shows what's happening now, while Analytics shows how the school is doing. At the top is a greeting, the date, and where you are in the term. Staff can clock in and out right here. Below that are your key numbers: students, staff, classes and the current term. Shortcuts take you straight to common jobs, like adding a student, importing a class from Excel, or inviting staff. Recent activity shows what your team did, and when. And orange numbers in the menu mean something is waiting for you, like a lesson note to approve.
e2-2: Everyone's overview fits their job. A class teacher sees a shorter menu, and only the shortcuts their role can use.
e2-3: Analytics compares this term with last term, and you can pick any term to look back on. You see the average score, pass rate, attendance and fees collected, each with its change. Hover over the chart for exact figures, and see which students need attention, and why.
e2-4: The Academics tab shows which subjects are strong and which need help. Narrow it to one class if you like. Subjects are listed weakest first. At the bottom, a table shows every class against every subject. Darker means higher scores.
e2-5: Students at risk are flagged before report cards go out, for low scores, falling grades or poor attendance. Filter by class or by reason, and open any student to see the full picture.
e2-6: The Teachers tab shows how each teacher is keeping up with score sheets, lesson notes and homework, least done first.
e3-1: Settings holds everything about how your school runs, grouped by area. This episode covers the School group.
e3-2: The school profile holds the details that appear on report cards, receipts and letters: the school's name, type and curriculum, its address, and the phone and email parents can reach. You also set the start of every admission number here. Upload your logo, and it appears on every page, report card, receipt and ID card. Then choose your school colour, from these swatches or by its code, check the preview, and save.
e3-4: Grading has its own episode. Under AI and Kola, you switch the AI helpers on or off for the whole school, and decide whether parents can ask Kola for help. You can see how many AI requests the school has used today. Each staff member gets thirty a day and each parent ten, and it resets at midnight.
e3-5: Web address lets you use your own school address, like portal dot adalin heights dot edu dot N G. Type it, save, then add the record shown here where your domain is managed. Click Check now to see if it's live. Your usual SchoolHub address keeps working either way.
e4-1: Payments is where school fees go. Enter the school's own bank account, and SchoolHub checks the account name with the bank for you. Once it's saved, parents' online payments go straight to the school, never through Adalin. Paystack takes its small fee per payment, and SchoolHub takes nothing. Collection rules decide how you follow up on what's owed. You can hold report cards until fees are paid, and send email reminders on weekday mornings. You can also add a note to print at the bottom of every invoice.
e4-2: Plan and billing shows your plan, what each plan includes, and your SchoolHub bills. Every plan is priced per student, per term. Upgrades start straight away. Moving to a cheaper plan starts next term, so nothing is lost in the middle of a term. You see the cost before you confirm. If you change your mind before next term, one click keeps you on your current plan. Your bills are listed below, one per term, based on the students on roll, and you can pay them online with Paystack. Questions about plans? Message Adalin on WhatsApp straight from here.
e4-3: Need help? You can let Adalin support into your school, only when you choose. Say what you need, pick twenty-four hours or three days, and access ends by itself. Every step support takes appears in your audit log.
e4-4: Add-ons are extras you can order without changing plan, like guided setup, on-site training or printed result PIN cards. What you order shows under Your add-ons.
e5-1: Messaging covers text message credits, automatic alerts to parents, and who can message whom. At the top is your credit balance, and what was sent in the last thirty days. Credits are bought in packs, and bigger packs cost less per message. Under alerts, choose what parents hear automatically. Absence alerts tell parents within minutes when a child is marked absent. Parents are also told when results are published, and every payment gets a receipt. Tick SMS to reach parents who aren't on the app. That uses credits. You can let parents message their child's class teacher, but only during set hours. Once your own sender name is registered, texts come from your school instead of SchoolHub. Save your settings. Recently sent lists every email and text, and failed texts are refunded.
e5-2: Admissions sets up your online application form. Switch it off, and the form tells parents admissions are closed. Choose which classes you're admitting into, and how you assess applicants: an entrance exam, an interview, either, or straight to an offer. You can charge a form fee, paid online, or leave it at zero. Add a welcome message and the exam details, then save. Share your admission link on WhatsApp, your website or social media. Open the form to see exactly what parents see. The full journey has its own episode.
e5-3: Staff and HR sets working hours for clocking in, and leave allowances. Set when the school day starts. Anyone who clocks in after the late time is marked late. Set closing time and the working days, and tick Saturday if staff come in then. Below, set how many days of each kind of leave staff get each year, like annual, sick and maternity leave. SchoolHub counts what's left whenever someone asks for leave. Then save.
e5-4: Payroll settings decide when staff are paid and what's deducted. Pick the pay day. PAYE tax uses the Nigeria Tax Act 2025 bands. Pension is eight percent from staff and ten percent from the school, and the housing fund is two and a half percent of basic pay. Paid payroll goes into Expenses automatically.
e5-5: Behaviour settings list the merits and incidents teachers can record, one per line. Then decide when parents hear about incidents: every one, only serious ones, or never. You can send good news too.
e5-5b: Library settings set the lending rules: how many days a book can be borrowed, how many books one person can have, and a fine for each day late. Inventory settings group the school's property into categories, like furniture and ICT, and list the rooms where things are kept. You can also choose to record the cost of new stock in Expenses.
e5-6: The sick bay settings list the medicines the school keeps, so the nurse picks from them. Choose when parents hear about a visit: after every visit, only when a child is sent home or referred, or never. Under transport, you can tell parents in the app when their child boards the school bus. Under boarding, parents can ask for an exeat in the app, and the warden approves it. Parents can also get a text when a boarder signs out and comes back.
e5-7: Documents settings decide who signs your certificates, testimonials and letters. For each signatory, add a name, a title like Principal, and a photo of their signature. Remove one, or add another. You can also add a note printed on the back of every ID card. Then save.
e6-1: Campuses lets you run several schools as one group. Each campus keeps its own students, staff and fees, and the group dashboard shows them side by side. Add a new campus by name, and it's set up on the group's plan. The dashboard itself is in the Enterprise episode.
e6-2: Staff sign-in can make staff use their school Google or Microsoft account instead of a password. Choose which accounts count. Proprietors can always use their password, so the school can never be locked out.
e6-3: API and webhooks connect SchoolHub to your website, accounting software or other systems. Developers will find every endpoint explained in the API documentation. API keys let another system read data from SchoolHub. A key can only read, and only from your school. Give the key a name, after the system that will use it, then tick exactly what it's allowed to read. When you create it, the full key is shown once only, so copy it into the other system straight away. Each key in the list shows what it can read and when it was last used. If a key is no longer needed, or you think it has leaked, revoke it. Anything using it stops working immediately. Webhooks work the other way round. SchoolHub tells your other systems the moment something happens. Enter the address to send messages to, then choose the events: a new student, a payment, or published results. You get a signing secret, also shown only once. Your system uses it to check that each message really came from SchoolHub. Send a test to make sure your system receives it. You can switch a webhook off for a while, or remove it completely. Every delivery is listed here, and any that fail are retried for about nine hours.
e6-4: Data and privacy. Your school's data belongs to your school. Download everything, students, staff, results, attendance and fees, as spreadsheets in one zip file. Passwords and PINs are left out. Adalin encrypts your data and never sells it. Every download is listed here.
e7-1: Academics is where you manage classes, subjects, teachers and terms. At the top is a quick count of classes, subjects and students, and the current term. Classes are grouped by level, and each level can have several arms, like Gold and Diamond. To add a class level, like Primary 4 or Year 7, give it a name, pick its section, and type its arms separated by commas. You can also add a new arm to a level that already exists. Here, JSS 1 Emerald is now ready for students. Each class has its own actions menu. From here you set the class teacher, who takes the register and writes report card comments, and how many students the class can take. Then save. You can remove a class you don't need, but a class with students must be emptied first.
e7-2: Subjects lists every subject the school teaches, and the classes that take it. To add one, type its name and tick the levels that offer it. Mark it as an elective if only some students take it. Only those students will get a score for it. Here, Robotics is added to the list. Edit a subject to change its name, code or classes. Or remove it, and it's taken off every class, along with its teachers.
e7-3: Subject teachers decide who teaches each subject in each class. Pick a class, then choose a teacher for each subject. It saves straight away, and that teacher now enters the scores.
e7-4: Electives shows which students take which optional subjects. Tick students one at a time, tick the whole class with All, or clear it with None. Save, and report cards will only show the subjects each student actually takes.
e7-5: Sessions and terms set the school year. For each term, set the date it resumes and the date it vacates. Report cards and the calendar use these dates. When a term ends, make the next one current. From then on, attendance, scores and fees all go against the new term. At the end of the year, start a new session, and its three terms are created for you. Then promote your students to their next class, which is covered in the Students episode.
e7-6: Assessment and grading set how each subject's score is made up. These are the columns teachers fill in. Here, two CAs of twenty marks each and an exam of sixty. You can start from a common split, like forty sixty or thirty seventy, or use four columns, and add your own, like a project. When you save, SchoolHub warns you first if any existing scores would be lost. Below is the grading scale. Use WAEC grades, A to F, British grades, or set your own: each grade, the lowest score that earns it, the remark on the report card, and whether it counts as a pass. Then save.
e8-1: Staff lists everyone who works at the school, and what each person can do. At the top: how many staff, who's active, invitations waiting, and the places your plan allows. Search by name, email or job title, filter by role or status, and export the list. Each person has an actions menu. Here we give Mrs Adeyemi a second role, Librarian. Roles decide which screens and buttons someone sees, and a person can have more than one. Now she has the Library in her menu, alongside her classes. Take a role away the same way. When someone leaves, deactivate them. They can no longer sign in, but their records stay. You can also download their data, or reactivate them later.
e8-2: To invite a new teacher, enter her details and choose her role, here Subject teacher. She gets an email invitation, and you can also send her the link on WhatsApp. Pending invitations are listed below. Each link works once and expires in seven days. Changed your mind? Cancel the invitation from its menu.
e8-3: Mrs Adeleke opens the link from her email. Her name is already filled in, so she just creates a password. She's in. As a subject teacher, she only sees what she needs: her classes, scores and lessons. Fees, payroll and settings belong to other roles.
e8-4: Roles and permissions show what each role can see and do. SchoolHub comes with the usual school roles, from Proprietor to Storekeeper. Parents and students have their own apps. Need a role that isn't there? Create your own, and tick exactly what it can do. You can only give permissions you have yourself. Here, an Exams officer role is ready to give to any staff member. Edit a role any time, and everyone with it gets the change straight away. Or delete it.
e9-1: Students lists every student in the school, with their class and parents. Search by name or admission number, show one class, or show students who've graduated, left or been suspended. You can export the list too. Each student has a menu, to view their profile, edit their details, mark them as graduated, suspend them, or withdraw them when they leave. Their records always stay. At the top are buttons to add a student, import a list from Excel, give students their own logins, and promote everyone at the end of the year. We'll go through each of these in this episode.
e9-2: Let's add a student. Kemi Adisa is joining JSS 1 Gold. Choose her class, and her admission number is created for you, with your school's prefix. Fill in her background, and the health details the nurse will need. Then add her parent. Her mother's email lets her sign in to the parent app. You can add a second parent, or use Save and add another when entering several students. Save, and Kemi's profile is ready, with her mother linked.
e9-3: Mrs Adisa opens the parent app and enters her email. No password needed. A code arrives by email, and she's in.
e9-4: A student's profile puts everything about Oluwaseun in one place. At the top are her fees, and any brothers or sisters at the school. From here you can change her status, message her parents, download her data, or edit her details. Under Parents and guardians, see who to contact. Mrs Lawal is the primary contact. Add or remove a parent here. If they already have a child at the school, they're linked, not duplicated. Class history shows every class, year by year. The Fees tab shows invoices and payments, where you can raise a one-off invoice or set a discount. Conduct shows merits and incidents, and Health holds the medical record and sick bay visits.
e9-5: Import brings in a whole class from Excel. Use our template, or your own list, and SchoolHub works out your column headings. Here's the school's list for the new JSS 1 Gold intake. Check the preview before anything is saved. Done: four new students, each with a parent and an admission number.
e9-6: Student logins let students do homework and CBT tests, and see their results. Pick a class, tick the students, or all of them, and issue logins. You get a slip for each student with the web address, school code, admission number and first password. Print them and hand them out.
e9-7: At the end of the school year, move everyone up a class in one go. First, set up the next session. Every student is set to move up, and SS 3 is set to graduate. Change a whole class at once, or one student, like Aisha, who's repeating JSS 1. Check the totals at the bottom, then confirm. Every student moves to their new class, and last year stays in their class history.
e10-1: Mr Adigun opens the school's admission link on his phone. The form shows the school's name, the form fee and the exam details. He fills in his daughter's details and his own, agrees to the school keeping them, and sends the form. The next page keeps him updated, and he gets the link by email too. He pays the form fee online, by card, transfer or USSD. The money goes straight to the school.
e10-2: Back at the school, Admissions lists every application as it comes in. Search by name, reference or phone, filter by class or by who has paid the form fee, and export the list. Ifeoluwa's application is in, with the fee paid. The next step is to invite her to the entrance exam, and her father is told by email. After the exam, record her score and any interview notes. If it's a no, mark the application not successful, or withdrawn if the family pulls out. Here it's a yes, so we offer admission. An offer letter is created with the school's logo and signature, and the parent sees the offer on their page.
e10-3: Mr Adigun gets an email saying Ifeoluwa has been offered a place. He downloads the letter, and accepts the offer.
e10-4: Now the school enrols Ifeoluwa. Choose her class and click Enrol. Her student record is created, with her father linked.
e11-1: It's eight in the morning. Mrs Adeyemi takes the register for her class on her phone. Everyone starts as present, so she only taps the few who aren't. Oluwaseun is absent. Ifeoluwa came in late, which still counts as present. Amina is excused, with a reason. She saves the register, and parents of absent children are told straight away.
e11-2: Minutes later, Mrs Lawal gets an alert, by email and in the parent app.
e11-3: The principal sees every class at once: how many registers are in, and who's in school, absent or late. Classes still to take their register stand out. Look back at any school day, or open a register to check or correct it.
e12-1: The timetable starts with the bell schedule: when each period starts and ends. Give it a name, choose the school days, and set each period's label, start time, end time and type, like lesson, break or assembly. Add periods as needed, then save. If the nursery finishes earlier, add another schedule, and choose which classes follow which.
e12-2: Each class has its own weekly timetable. The panel shows how many lessons each subject has, and here all forty lessons are placed. Click any period to set its lesson. The teacher fills in by itself from Subject teachers. You can add a room, or a note like Library period. If the teacher is busy with another class at that time, SchoolHub warns you. To swap two lessons, drag one onto the other. Each term can have its own timetable, and you can print it for the classroom wall.
e12-3: Pick a teacher to see their week. Teachers and students see their own timetables when they sign in.
e13-1: Results shows every class's scores and report cards. Each class moves through four steps: scores in, reviewed, approved and published. Let's follow JSS 1 Diamond from scores all the way to parents.
e13-2: Mr Obi teaches maths. Each student has a box for each CA and the exam. He types a score, and it saves by itself, even if the internet drops. Totals, grades and positions work themselves out. When the whole class is done, he submits the sheet to the class teacher.
e13-3: Mrs Adeyemi is the class teacher. She checks the class before it goes to the principal. Subject sheets show which teachers have submitted. The broadsheet shows every student and every subject on one page, and it can be exported to Excel. Under report cards, she sees each student's position and average, and writes a comment for each child. Stuck for words? Kola can suggest one from the child's results, and she can change anything she likes. Then she rates behaviour and skills, and saves. The preview shows the finished report card, with the school's logo, every subject, the comments and the ratings. When she's done, she marks the class as reviewed for the principal.
e13-4: Dr Ogunleye, the principal, sees that JSS 1 Diamond has been reviewed. The principal adds a comment too. If something's wrong, send it back to the teachers. If it's right, approve and lock it, so scores can't be changed. Then publish to parents, adding the date next term begins, which is printed on every report card. Parents get an email, and see the report card in the app. You can print the whole class's report cards in one file. And if you find a mistake later, unlock, fix it, and publish again.
e14-1: Result PINs work like scratch cards, so parents can check results online without an account. Share the result checker link, or print it on the cards. Choose how many PINs, and how many times each can be used. Each PIN locks to the first student it's used for, so it can't be passed around. PINs are shown only once, so download them as a spreadsheet or print the cards. Each card shows the school's name, the term, the PIN, a serial number and the link.
e14-2: A parent opens the result checker on their phone, and types the admission number and the PIN from the card. A mistyped PIN gets a clear message. With the right PIN, the report card opens straight away, ready to save or print.
e15-1: Assignments covers homework and classwork for every class you teach. You can see what's open, what's due this week, and what's waiting to be marked, and filter by class, subject or status. To set a new assignment, choose when it's due and what it's marked out of, and count it towards a CA if you like. You can accept late work, which is flagged as late, and attach worksheets or pictures. Save it as a draft, or set it, and students see it straight away. Parents can see it too.
e15-2: Oluwaseun sees the new homework in her student app, with the instructions and due date. She types her answer, attaches a photo of her exercise book, and hands it in.
e15-3: Back with Mr Obi, he sees who has handed in, who's late, and the class average. Switch between handed in, left to mark, and not handed in. He opens Oluwaseun's work, gives a mark and a comment, and saves. She sees them in her app. An assignment set by mistake can be deleted.
e15-4: Lesson notes start with the scheme of work: the topic for each week of the term, planned by subject and class level. Under My notes, Mr Obi sees every lesson note he has written, and where each one stands. For a new lesson note, the class, subject and week come from his timetable. He can type it, or attach a note written by hand, scanned or photographed. Save it as a draft, or send it for approval.
e15-5: The principal sees every teacher's notes, approved, waiting or returned. Open a note waiting for approval, read it and leave a comment. Then send it back for changes, or approve it. The teacher is told either way.
e16-1: CBT exams start with the question bank: questions you write once and use again. To add one by hand, type the question and four options, tick the right answer, and set the marks. Theory questions are marked by the teacher. You can also paste questions from Word, or from a photo of a past paper. Or let Kola write some for you. Give it a topic, and it writes five questions with the answers marked. Read them, change anything, then add them to the bank.
e16-2: Exams lists every test, when it opens, and how many students have finished. For a new test, choose the class, add instructions, and set how long students get. Set when it opens and closes. Students can only start within that window. Count it towards a CA if you like, shuffle the questions to stop copying, and show students their score at the end. Pick questions from the bank, then save a draft or schedule it.
e16-3: Oluwaseun's test is open now. She sees how many questions there are, how long she has, and the rules. Questions come one at a time, with a countdown clock, and answers save as she goes. All questions shows what's answered and what's left. She submits, and sees her score straight away.
e16-4: Mr Obi sees every score as students finish, with no marking for objective questions. He can give one student more time, change the closing time, or close the test now. The Questions tab shows how many students got each one right. For written answers, open each script, enter a mark, and save.
e17-1: Learning materials hold notes, worksheets and videos for your classes. You can share files, links and videos, and YouTube plays inside the app. You can also write typed notes. Search, or filter by class, subject and type. To share something new, choose a file like slides, PDFs or worksheets from your computer, a link to YouTube or a website, or a typed note. Share it, and every student in the class can open it. Each item can be edited or removed later.
e17-2: Oluwaseun finds everything her teachers shared, sorted by subject.
e18-1: Behaviour records merits for good behaviour, and incidents when something goes wrong. At the top are this term's merits and incidents, open serious cases, and how many parents were told. Click Record to add a merit, or an incident. For an incident, choose what kind it was and how serious. Save it. For moderate and serious incidents, parents are told automatically. The log lists everything recorded, newest first. And the leaderboard shows the students and classes with the most merits this term.
e18-2: Mrs Lawal is told straight away.
e18-3: The library shows every book, how many copies are on the shelf, and who has them. To add a book, type its ISBN and look it up, and the details fill in for you. Choose its category, the number of copies, and which shelf it sits on. To lend a book, pick a student or a member of staff, and set when it's due back. Late books build up a fine, if you've set one. Loans shows who has what and when it's due, and overdue books stand out. When a book comes back, press Returned.
e19-1: Transport lists the school's bus routes, each with its stops, times and bus. Add a route with its stops and pick-up times. Under Students, assign who rides which bus. Here, Ifeoluwa goes on the Lekki to Ajah bus, with her stop, and mornings, afternoons or both. Buses shows each driver, attendant and free seats. On the bus register, the attendant ticks who got on, and parents are told in the app.
e19-2: Boarding shows each hostel, its rooms, and how many beds are free. Add a hostel and its rooms. Under Boarders, Ifeoluwa gets a bed in Queen Amina House. Leave the bed number blank, and SchoolHub picks the first free bed. Exeats give permission to leave school. Parents can ask in the app, or the warden can record one, like a weekend at home for Chukwuemeka. Set when the student leaves and when they must be back. Late returns are flagged, and parents are told when a boarder signs out and comes back.
e19-3: The sick bay shows who's resting now, and today's visits. Oluwaseun comes in with a headache. Her allergies and conditions show up before anything is given. The nurse records any medicine from the school's list, with the dose, and how she left: back to class, still resting, sent home or referred. All visits are listed below. Health records hold each student's allergies, conditions, medication, and who to call in an emergency.
e19-4: Mrs Lawal is told straight away.
e20-1: Announcements share news with parents, students and staff, in the app and by email. Each one shows how many parents have read it. To post a new one, choose who it's for: everyone, parents, students, some classes, or staff only. Tick email to send it to every family, or text message, which uses credits. Pin it to keep it first. Once posted, parents see it straight away.
e20-2: Mrs Lawal sees it in the app.
e20-3: The calendar holds term dates, holidays, exams and events, for staff and parents. Move between months with the arrows. To add an event, give it a title and date, and choose whether parents can see it or it's for staff only. Save, and it's on the calendar and in the parent app.
e20-4: Messages are private conversations between teachers and parents. Here, Mrs Adeyemi writes to Oluwaseun's parents. She types her message and sends it. The parent gets it in the app, and by email too.
e20-5: Mrs Lawal opens the message in her parent app, and replies.
e20-6: Mrs Adeyemi sees the reply waiting. The whole conversation is kept in one place, and parents can only message during the hours you set.
e21-1: Fees shows what's been billed this term, what's been paid, and what's still owed, with collections week by week. At the start of term, raise everyone's invoices in one go from the fee structure, for every class or only some. Students who already have an invoice are skipped, so nobody is billed twice.
e21-2: The fee structure lists each fee item, and what each class level pays this term. Add an item, like a development levy, or copy last term's amounts. Make items like the bus optional, then save.
e21-3: Invoices lists every student's bill for the term. Filter by unpaid, part paid, paid or overdue, and export to Excel. Here's Ifeoluwa's new invoice, with each fee item, any discount, and what's left to pay. You can add a one-off charge, like a lost book, or give a discount. Email the parent a reminder from here, or copy the payment link to send on WhatsApp. Download the invoice as a PDF, with the school's logo and bank details. Her father paid part of it in cash at the school, so we record the payment. It gets a numbered receipt, which the parent also gets by email. The receipt is ready to print. An invoice raised by mistake can be voided. Nothing is ever deleted.
e21-4: Mr Adigun opens the payment link on his phone. No account needed. He sees what's owed, chooses to pay all or part, and pays by card, transfer or USSD. The money goes straight to the school, and the receipt is emailed.
e21-5: Payments lists every payment, cash or online, with its receipt number. Filter, and export for the accountant.
e21-6: Debtors shows who still owes, how much, and when they were last reminded. Show only overdue invoices, tick the families to remind, and send an email with their balance and payment link. Or remind everyone at once. Automatic reminders can be switched on in Settings.
e21-7: Discounts and scholarships are set up once and used every term. Choose a percentage off, or a fixed amount, on all compulsory fees or on one item like tuition. Then give it to a student from the Fees tab on their profile, and their invoices update.
e22-1: Expenses records everything the school spends, by category. You see what was spent this month, what's waiting for approval, and the biggest cost. The bursar records a purchase, and it waits for the proprietor's approval.
e22-2: The proprietor sees what's waiting, opens its menu, and approves it, or rejects it with a reason. The income statement shows fees in, spending out, and the surplus or deficit, for any period.
e22-3: Payroll starts with each person's pay: basic salary, allowances like housing and transport, and deductions like a loan repayment. PAYE, pension and the housing fund are worked out for you. Each month, prepare payroll in one click. November's draft shows every payslip, with gross pay, deductions and take-home, plus what to transfer to staff and remit to the tax office. You can adjust one person's pay for a bonus or overtime.
e22-4: The proprietor checks the draft and approves it, which locks the payslips. Once the transfers have gone out, mark it as paid. Staff are told their payslips are ready, and the cost goes into Expenses.
e22-5: Mrs Adeyemi opens My payslips to see her pay, allowances, deductions and take-home.
e23-1: This is Mrs Adeyemi's day on her phone. Staff clock in here when they arrive, and clock out at the end of the day. She can see her leave balance and ask for time off, choosing the type of leave. The principal is told.
e23-2: The principal sees who's in, who's late, and who's on leave today, and can mark someone by hand. The monthly view shows each person's days on time, late and absent. Under leave requests, Mrs Adeyemi's annual leave is waiting. Decline it with a reason, or approve it, and she's told straight away.
e23-3: Approved, and her leave balance updates.
e24-1: Documents covers ID cards, testimonials, transcripts, certificates and letters, each with a QR code. Make student ID cards for a whole class. Every card has the photo, class, admission number, and a QR code to check it's real. Staff ID cards work the same way, ready to print.
e24-2: For a student who's leaving, make a testimonial. Their years at the school fill in, and you add what you'd like to say. The testimonial is signed and numbered. A transcript lists every term's results, taken from published report cards, ready to send to another school or university.
e24-3: Certificates come from your own templates, for a whole class or chosen students, each with its own serial number. Letters to parents can be a resumption notice, an invitation, or your own wording. Each letter is addressed to the child's parents, on the school's letterhead.
e24-4: The register lists every document the school has issued, with its serial number. Filter by kind, like ID cards. Reprint a lost card, and it keeps the same code. Check opens the page its QR code leads to. If a card is stolen, revoke it, and its QR code shows it's no longer valid. Under templates, write your own certificates and letters. Give it a name and write the wording. The student's name and class fill in by themselves.
e24-5: Anyone can scan the QR code to confirm the document is genuine.
e25-1: Inventory tracks everything the school owns, from chalk to projectors. You see what's in the store, what's running low, and what's signed out. To add something new, choose whether it gets used up, like chalk and paper, or it's kept and signed out, like a projector. Set the reorder level, and it shows as running low at that number. Issue items to a teacher or a room, and the count goes down by itself. When a delivery arrives, stock it in, and its cost can go straight to Expenses. After a stock count, record the new number and why it changed. Items can be edited or removed.
e25-2: Signed out shows equipment with staff or in rooms. Check items back in, and History shows every move.
e25-3: The audit log shows who did what, and when, across the whole school. Sensitive changes are flagged. Search, or filter by area. The storekeeper's change a moment ago is already here. Nothing here can be edited or deleted.
e26-1: Kola is SchoolHub's helper, on every page. Ask anything about using SchoolHub, or start with a quick question, like what can I do on this page. Kola knows which page you're on, and answers with the steps and a link. Ask a follow-up, like you would a colleague. Kola only helps with SchoolHub, and never changes anything for you.
e26-2: Teachers can ask Kola on their phones too. Kola answers for their role, so a class teacher gets class teacher steps.
e26-3: Parents have Kola in the parent app. It explains how to pay fees, check results and message the school.
e26-4: In the question bank, AI can turn a photo of a past paper into questions. Every question and option is typed out for you, with answers to check. Check them, then add them to the bank. Nothing personal is ever sent.
e26-5: Importing a list with unusual headings? The AI works out which column is which. Only the headings are sent, never the names. Check the preview, then import.
e27-1: This is the parent app. Mrs Lawal has two children at the school. She sees everything about Oluwaseun at a glance: attendance for every day this term, homework, the timetable, merits and incidents, and sick bay visits. Under fees, each invoice, with a button to pay. And under results, each term's report card, the same one the school prints.
e27-2: Some schools hold report cards until fees are paid. Here, Oluwaseun lost a textbook, so the bursar adds a small charge.
e27-3: Now Mrs Lawal's report card is held. She pays the twelve thousand, five hundred naira from her phone, and it opens again.
e27-4: Under messages, she writes to her child's class teacher, with a subject and a message. Updates lists every alert, newest first. Account holds her details, and how she'd like to hear from the school, by text or WhatsApp.
e28-1: Students sign in with the slip their school gave them. Today shows their attendance, the day's lessons, and news from the school.
e28-2: The student app has a weekly timetable, homework, exams, and materials from teachers. Results shows her published report cards, if the school allows it. The library shows the books she has, and when they're due. Under account, she can change her password, and sign out on a shared phone.
e29-1: Enterprise is for groups of schools. Adalin Heights runs campuses in Ikoyi and Abuja, and a third is opening in Lekki. Add the campus, and it's set up on the group's plan. The group dashboard shows students, staff, attendance and fees across every campus, and Lekki is already there.
e29-2: Staff sign-in can require every staff member to use their school Google or Microsoft account.
e29-4: The API connects your website or accounting system. Every request uses a key, and only reads what that key allows. Webhooks tell your systems the moment something happens. That's the whole of SchoolHub. Questions? Ask Kola, or WhatsApp Adalin.
e30-1: Here's a brand-new school. Let's finish the setup checklist, one step at a time. Step one: the school profile, with its type, phone and address. Step two: classes. Tick the sections, name the arms, and set the session. Set up my school creates every class, the common Nigerian subjects, and three terms. Step three: invite a teacher. Step four: add a student. With all four steps done, the checklist makes way for the school's everyday overview.
e30-2: Forgot your password? Staff can reset it themselves. A reset link is emailed, and it works once, for a short time. The link opens this page to choose a new password. Save it, and you're signed straight in.
e30-3: A test that hasn't opened yet can still be changed: its time, dates or questions.
e30-4: Finally, the small print: the terms of use in plain English, the privacy notice, and the data processing agreement every school accepts.
